forensic_summary: Trigger: Urgent need for functional prototypes (Zeus Server, Pluto Node) for CES. Intervention: The Architect completed Zeus ProE files solo and managed the fabrication with EMS. Result: Enclosures delivered and functional tests running prior to CES.

scars.description: With a hard deadline for the Consumer Electronics Show (CES), I executed the mechanical design for the 'Zeus' TVNET server and 'Pluto' node in isolation. Working as a solo contractor (Mechanistic), I delivered production-ready Pro/ENGINEER files to EMS and coordinated the fabrication of prototype units with Sputnik Models. The units were delivered and functional for the show floor demonstration.
scars.label: The CES Sprint

scars.description: During the 9-day fabrication window, I executed real-time DXF swaps with the PCB team to detect a mounting hole collision with the Compact Flash card (Titan Node). Caught the crash in digital space before metal was cut, preventing a line-down scenario.
scars.label: The Titan Node Collision

scars.description: Legacy design had ventilation holes under the heat spreader, killing conduction. I executed a 'surgical strike' to eliminate the holes and specced thermopad gap fillers to bridge the physical gap, admitting 'dead nuts flat' is a fantasy.
scars.label: The Thermal Contradiction

scars.description: Eliminated the metric/imperial chaos on the assembly line by mandating a global purge of all metric hardware. Standardized entire chassis on 4-40 UNC to increase assembly velocity during the crunch.
scars.label: Draconian Standardization
